mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases real discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% y/y, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates labor market tightening coupled with monetary policy tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: labor market tightening with monetary policy tightening
failure_condition: The negative correlation between the joint signal (UNRATE decline and FEDFUNDS rise) and S&P 500 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial contraction (INDPRO decline), manufacturing sector weakness reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of INDPRO decline, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) consistently increases real discount rates, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day S&P 500 returns is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE is below 4.0%, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates broad economic slowdown, reducing corporate revenue growth and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The negative correlation between the joint signal (HOUST decline and INDPRO decline) and S&P 500 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong labor market expansion (PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.3% monthly), rising consumer spending drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods of PAYEMS growth above 0.3% monthly, S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
